chunks: From him, from al-Sayyari, raising it (to the Imam), said:

Meats were mentioned in front of Umar, so Umar said, 'The best of the meats is the meat of the chicken.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said, 'No! Those are the pigs of the birds, and the best of the meats is the meat of a chick that has risen (stood up) or is near to rising.'

key_terms.خَنَازِيرُ الطَّيْرِ: Pigs of the birds (a metaphorical description for chickens)
key_terms.نَهَضَ: Risen/Stood up (referring to the chick's development)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) say about the quality of chicken meat compared to other birds?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) refutes Umar’s preference for mature chicken by metaphorically labeling them 'the pigs of the birds,' likely due to their omnivorous diet and lack of selective eating. He elevates the status of the young chick (*farakh*) that has just gained strength, establishing a distinct Shia culinary and scholarly perspective on poultry quality that contrasts with the companion's view. This highlights the Imam’s attention to both the physical vitality and the dietary purity of the animal as criteria for the best meat.
